signals.text: 4 open PM roles across 1 US office

bullets: Lead product development for tuition payments and other provider-facing financial tools
Grow total payments volume, product adoption, and net revenue
Improve provider NPS and reduce friction across the billing experience
Drive profitability and improve unit economics through product and pricing strategy
Work end-to-end with engineering, design, and data to ship features weekly
Design and scale a SaaS platform for early childhood state agencies and their operational teams
Build data tools and workflows that enable leaders to understand supply, demand, funding, and usage
Integrate Wonderschool’s government tools seamlessly with the provider and family platforms
Deliver features that support compliance, subsidy management, policy reporting, and real-time dashboards
Co-design solutions with government users to ensure engagement, usability, and real-world value
Map customer and internal workflows to find where an agent can complete a useful task or help a person do it faster.
Define each agent’s job, tool access, decision boundaries, escalation path, and success measures.
Partner with engineering, design, and operations to prototype, launch, and improve agent systems.
Build evaluations and review real failures, customer feedback, and operational data to understand where agents succeed or struggle.
Track quality, reliability, latency, cost, adoption, and customer outcomes; use those signals to prioritize improvements.
Own the payments product roadmap with a dedicated payments team: banking, cards, Stripe, SAP, partner advances, payroll, and our billing platform
Consolidate and simplify a payments platform assembled from many legacy system integrations
Work hands-on with the fintech partners who power most of our payment capabilities, and own the integration and reconciliation/tracking layer across them
Spend significant time with customers to understand how money actually moves for them and where it breaks
Partner daily with engineering to build, ship, measure, and iterate
